`abstract class Texture`<br/>
**Implements:** [`ITexture`](/reference/bridges/itexture/)<br/>
**Known subtypes:** [`GlTexture`](/reference/base-opengl/gltexture/), [`VulkanTexture`](/reference/vulkan/vulkantexture/)<br/>
**Package:** `dev.joid.lib.bridge.render.texture` · **Module:** `core` · **Source:** [Texture.java](https://github.com/Zeldown/JOID/blob/main/core/src/main/java/dev/joid/lib/bridge/render/texture/Texture.java)

The base class of a texture owned by JOID, which checks every call and leaves the storage, the upload and the mipmaps to its subclass.

- [Textures](/build/writing-a-backend/#textures)

<a id="Texture-method-allocate"></a>

### allocate

`this allocate(int width, int height)` <span class="joid-qualifier">fluent</span>

**Throws:**

- `IllegalStateException`: The texture is deleted, create a new one with IRenderBridge.createTexture()

Allocates the storage at that size, with every level when mipmapped; does nothing when the size and the levels are already those.
Throws an `IllegalStateException` once the texture is deleted.

<a id="Texture-method-upload"></a>

### upload

`this upload(int[] pixels)` <span class="joid-qualifier">fluent</span>

**Throws:**

- `IllegalStateException`: The texture is deleted, create a new one with IRenderBridge.createTexture()
- `IllegalStateException`: The texture is not allocated, call allocate(width, height) before upload(pixels)
- `IllegalArgumentException`: The texture of …x… needs … pixels and got …, pass one pixel per texel

Uploads one ARGB pixel per texel and builds the mipmaps.
Throws an `IllegalStateException` before `allocate` or once deleted, and an `IllegalArgumentException` with fewer pixels than texels.

<a id="Texture-method-delete"></a>

### delete

`void delete()` 

Releases the storage; does nothing the second time.

<a id="Texture-method-getMaxLevels"></a>

### getMaxLevels

`int getMaxLevels(int width, int height)` <span class="joid-qualifier">hook</span> <span class="joid-qualifier">protected</span>

JOID calls it before each allocation and upload.
Return the most levels your API gives a texture of that size; no limit by default.

<a id="Texture-method-allocateStorage"></a>

### allocateStorage

`void allocateStorage(MipmapChain chain)` <span class="joid-qualifier">hook</span> <span class="joid-qualifier">abstract</span> <span class="joid-qualifier">protected</span>

JOID calls it from `allocate`.
Allocate every level of the chain; throw an `IllegalArgumentException` that starts with `A texture of <width>x<height> exceeds the maximum size` when the size is too large.

<a id="Texture-method-uploadPixels"></a>

### uploadPixels

`void uploadPixels(int[] pixels, MipmapChain chain)` <span class="joid-qualifier">hook</span> <span class="joid-qualifier">abstract</span> <span class="joid-qualifier">protected</span>

JOID calls it from `upload`.
Write the pixels into the first level, then build the other levels of the chain.

<a id="Texture-method-generateMipmapLevels"></a>

### generateMipmapLevels

`void generateMipmapLevels(MipmapChain chain, int allocatedLevels)` <span class="joid-qualifier">hook</span> <span class="joid-qualifier">abstract</span> <span class="joid-qualifier">protected</span>

JOID calls it when mipmaps are turned on for an allocated texture, with the number of levels already allocated.
Allocate the missing levels and build them from the first one.

<a id="Texture-method-deleteStorage"></a>

### deleteStorage

`void deleteStorage()` <span class="joid-qualifier">hook</span> <span class="joid-qualifier">abstract</span> <span class="joid-qualifier">protected</span>

JOID calls it once, from `delete()`.
Release the storage.
